title.narrative: Integrated Life Saving Assistance: Improving Immediate Nutrition and Health Outcomes for Vulnerable Communities in Jere, Bama, and Ngala LGAs.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe proposed Integrated Life-Saving Project seeks to urgently address the critical nutrition, health, and protection needs of 45,000 conflict-affected individuals (15,750 women, 13,500 girls, 6750 men, and 9,000 boys) across Bama, Jere, and Ngala LGAs of Borno State, Nigeria. These LGAs remain at the epicenter of the protracted humanitarian crisis in the Northeast, where communities continue to experience widespread food insecurity, rising malnutrition, poor access to healthcare, and heightened protection concerns. Women, children, and persons with disabilities face particularly severe challenges as conflict, displacement, and poverty limit their ability to meet basic survival needs.ltbrgtRecent assessments indicate that Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates across BAY states have risen to 19.9 percent, with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) at 9.2 percent, both well above emergency thresholds, signaling immediate risk of mortality among children. Women and girls in these LGAs face extraordinary risks. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) in northeastern Nigeria is estimated at 1,549 deaths per 100,000 live births, among the highest globally. These statistics underline the importance of urgent, integrated interventions.ltbrgtProject Goal: To provide immediate health, and nutrition needs to the most vulnerable people in Bama, Jere, and Ngala LGAs by delivering quality, accessible, and gender-responsive life-saving services.ltbrgtNutrition: The project will scale up active case finding and referral of acute malnutrition cases through community-based volunteers and health workers. Children suffering from MAM will receive treatment using RUSF/Tom Brown, while caregivers will be supported with Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling to improve feeding practices. Supplementary food assistance will be provided for children aged 6-23 months to reduce the risk of deterioration into severe malnutrition. Nutrition service delivery platforms will also integrate GBV/PSEA awareness messaging to improve protection linkages.ltbrgtHealth: The health component will ensure access to integrated primary healthcare services covering routine immunization, antenatal and postnatal care, treatment of common illnesses such as malaria and pneumonia, and provision of MHPSS. Strengthened referral systems will link community health workers with primary facilities and secondary care centers for timely case management. Women and adolescent girls will be prioritized for sexual and reproductive health services, including safe delivery, emergency obstetric care, family planning, and GBV-sensitive clinical services. The project will also reinforce disease outbreak preparedness and response, addressing seasonal threats such as cholera, measles, and malaria.ltbrgtProtection (GBV): The protection component will focus on lifesaving GBV mainstreaming activities. At the facility and nutrition delivery, sensitization campaigns will raise awareness of GBV risks, promote reporting mechanisms, and engage men, boys, and community leaders in shifting harmful practices. The project will also advocate with other sectors, such as food security and livelihoods, to reduce negative coping mechanisms like survival sex and child labor.lt/pgtltpgtOutcomesltbrgt1. Increased access to quality, gender-responsive malnutrition prevention and treatment services, particularly for children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls.ltbrgt2. Strengthened community-led systems for the prevention, identification, and referral of malnutrition and GBV cases.ltbrgt3. Improved access to integrated and essential healthcare services, including sexual and reproductive health and MHPSS.ltbrgt4. Strengthened AAP and disability-inclusive approaches across all project components.ltbrgtlt/pgt
